Aside from distance of lightning, what else determines the loudness of thunder?
Thunder is just sound waves. So air density and the presence of sound deadening objects I imagine. I have no sources for this though, this is just what I assume from basic physics.

You're correct! All sound is just a pressure wave thru the air, so thunder loudness (and distance traveled) depends on where you are and air conditions.

Sound travels faster when the medium is denser, so it will travel a little further at sea level than it would at high altitude. Not by much though.

Local geography would also affect it. Sound cant propagate through a mountain very well, so it goes around. However since the source of the sound is so large (literally a column of air snapping from ground to cloud), man-made things like buildings arent big enough to make much of a difference.

Source: I work in audio
